chunks.title: Simple Herbed Couscous
chunks.text:
Couscous is a North African staple made from steamed semolina. This quick version
is ready in about ten minutes and pairs with almost anything.

- 1 cup couscous
- 1 cup boiling water or stock
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- A handful of chopped parsley and mint
- Salt and lemon juice to taste
chunks.summary: Couscous is a North African staple made from steamed semolina.

chunks.title: Simple Herbed Couscous
chunks.text:
Place the couscous in a bowl and pour the boiling stock over it. Cover immediately
and let it sit undisturbed for five minutes. The grains absorb the liquid and
steam in their own heat.

Fluff with a fork to separate the grains, then fold in the olive oil, herbs, salt,
and a squeeze of lemon. Serve warm or at room temperature.
chunks.summary: Place the couscous in a bowl and pour the boiling stock over it.

chunks.title: Kimura Grip Mechanics from Closed Guard
chunks.text:
The kimura, also called the double wristlock, is a shoulder lock attacked from
many positions. From closed guard it begins with wrist control on the opponent's
posting arm.
chunks.summary:
The kimura, also called the double wristlock, is a shoulder lock attacked from
many positions.

chunks.title: Kimura Grip Mechanics from Closed Guard
chunks.text:
When the opponent answers the phone to defend the kimura, the critical mechanic
is driving your elbow toward their far hip rather than trying to muscle the arm
backward. Muscling the arm fights their entire body; the elbow drive isolates the
shoulder joint and removes their leverage.

Establish the figure-four grip first. Your near hand grips their wrist, your far
hand threads under their arm and grips your own wrist. This is the control frame.
chunks.summary:
When the opponent answers the phone to defend the kimura, the critical mechanic
is driving your elbow toward their far hip rather than trying to muscle the arm
backward.

chunks.title: Kimura Grip Mechanics from Closed Guard
chunks.text:
Rotate their forearm toward the back of their head while keeping your elbows
tight. Hip escape slightly to create the angle. The finish is slow and positional,
never a jerk.
chunks.summary:
Rotate their forearm toward the back of their head while keeping your elbows
tight.

chunks.title: Minnesota Facts
chunks.text:
Minnesota is a state in the upper midwestern United States. Its largest city is
Minneapolis, which together with the neighboring capital, Saint Paul, forms the
Twin Cities metropolitan area.
chunks.summary: Minnesota is a state in the upper midwestern United States.

chunks.title: Minnesota Facts
chunks.text:
Minnesota is known as the Land of 10,000 Lakes. The actual count of lakes ten
acres or larger is closer to 11,842. The Mississippi River begins at Lake Itasca
in the northern part of the state.
chunks.summary: Minnesota is known as the Land of 10,000 Lakes.

chunks.title: Minnesota Facts
chunks.text:
Minnesota winters are long and cold. International Falls, on the Canadian border,
is often the coldest spot in the lower 48 states and bills itself as the Icebox
of the Nation.
chunks.summary: Minnesota winters are long and cold.
